We are a 6-member research team taking on the CLPS Lunar Mission Browser! 

🌑 Team: Pouya, Larissa, Lucky, Sameera, Aparna & Pranjal. 

 We're creating an interactive web tool that computes Sun/Earth geometry ☀️, illumination & solar power potential ⚡, and direct-to-Earth communication windows 📡 for lunar south pole landing sites. It is powered by real NASA ephemeris & terrain data. 🎨 Looking for: UI/UX designers & web devs! 🚀

summary:
**Lunar Window SI** is an interactive, physics-guided decision-support application developed by Team SHE ORBITS for NASA's Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge.

Landing near the Moon's south pole requires balancing solar illumination, direct-to-Earth communication, and mission timing. Even small changes in landing schedules or horizon assumptions can significantly affect operational availability.

Our web application enables users to explore candidate lunar locations, visualize Sun and Earth positions, evaluate overlapping illumination and communication windows, and compare landing scenarios.

Our key innovation is **Delay-Resilient Landing Intelligence**: instead of evaluating only a fixed landing date, the system investigates what happens when a mission is delayed by three days or more. A lightweight Gaussian Process and Bayesian optimization algorithm searches for promising alternative locations, which are subsequently evaluated using physics-based calculations.

The prototype emphasizes transparent assumptions, interactive scientific visualization, and explainable recommendations. It provides an accessible framework for preliminary mission screening, education, and future integration of high-resolution NASA lunar terrain and ephemeris data.
details:
Lunar Window SI — Project Details

1. The Challenge

Future lunar missions, particularly those targeting the Moon's south pole, must operate in environments with challenging illumination, complex terrain, and changing Earth visibility. A landing site suitable for one date may become operationally unfavorable after a launch or landing delay.

Existing scientific tools provide valuable ephemeris and lunar mapping capabilities, but rapidly combining terrain, sunlight, communication visibility, and mission schedule changes remains challenging.

2. Our Solution

Team SHE ORBITS developed Lunar Window AI, an interactive web-based environment that transforms scientific lunar datasets and geometric calculations into visual, explainable mission-planning information.

The platform includes:

  • An interactive 3D lunar terrain and celestial visualization environment.
  • Custom landing coordinates and UTC date selection.
  • Sun and Earth azimuth and elevation calculations.
  • Terrain-aware horizon analysis at supported lunar locations.
  • Solar illumination and direct-to-Earth geometric visibility assessments.
  • Simultaneous operational-window and blackout-duration analysis.
  • Comparison of scheduled and delayed landing scenarios.
  • AI-assisted exploration of alternative landing locations.
  • Preliminary celestial-bearing geometry analysis for attitude acquisition.

3. Scientific Methodology

The application combines multiple scientific components.

Lunar terrain: Digital elevation products from NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) are used to construct local terrain representations and directional horizon profiles for four example south-polar locations.

Celestial geometry: The application calculates Sun and Earth directions in a Moon-fixed reference frame and transforms them into local azimuth and elevation coordinates. Archived JPL Horizons observations provide an independent reference for checking angular calculations.

Mission-window analysis: For each scenario, the system evaluates the availability of sunlight, geometric Earth visibility, and their overlap. The selected mission is reevaluated across different landing delays and horizon-clearance assumptions.

Navigation observability: A preliminary two-vector attitude-information model evaluates the geometric conditioning of simultaneous Sun and Earth measurements, considering assumed angular measurement precision and required acquisition duration.

4. Artificial Intelligence

The platform incorporates lightweight, physics-guided Bayesian optimization using Gaussian Process regression with a radial basis function kernel and an Upper Confidence Bound acquisition strategy.

The algorithm explores candidate locations, estimates promising regions, and prioritizes further physical-model evaluations. Recommendations are based on computed objective values rather than unsupported AI predictions.

The search evaluates operational resilience under schedule changes. Its output is a transparent planning preference, not a probability of successful landing.

5. Core Innovation

Our central contribution is Delay-Resilient Landing Intelligence.

Rather than assessing a landing site only at a nominal arrival time, Lunar Window examines how its operational suitability changes when mission timing shifts.

A complementary innovation is Navigation-Aware Window Assessment, which distinguishes basic Sun–Earth visibility from intervals where two celestial bearings provide sufficiently well-conditioned geometry under an explicitly assumed sensor model.

This distinction is important because simultaneous visibility does not automatically guarantee adequate navigation observability.

The platform brings these considerations into one interactive environment, allowing users to explore engineering trade-offs rather than viewing isolated astronomical quantities.

6. Scientific Validation and Limitations

The repository includes 488 archived JPL Horizons body/site/time reference records and documented comparisons with the application's celestial-direction calculations.

A reproducible research example shows how two candidate locations with comparable nominal joint visibility can have different navigation-qualified windows when terrain, timing, and measurement assumptions are considered.

The prototype is intended for preliminary evaluation and education, not certified flight operations. Terrain-aware calculations are available for the preprocessed example locations; other coordinates use an explicitly identified simplified horizon model. The application does not calculate complete electrical power budgets, radio-link performance, landing hazards, or verified onboard attitude-estimation errors.

7. Expected Impact

Lunar Window could help mission designers, researchers, students, and educators understand the relationships between lunar terrain, celestial geometry, operational timing, and navigation constraints.

Its principal value is making scenario changes interpretable: users can examine not only whether a site appears favorable, but how robust that assessment is when schedules and engineering assumptions change.

The project provides a reproducible starting point for future integration of higher-resolution terrain, uncertainty-aware planning, and mission-specific power, communications, and navigation models.

8. Technologies and Resources

The project uses HTML, CSS, JavaScript, SVG and browser-based visualization, the Astronomy Engine ephemeris library, Gaussian Process regression, Bayesian optimization, NASA LOLA terrain products, NASA lunar imagery, and JPL Horizons reference observations.

The application is designed to run as a lightweight web platform without requiring a paid AI service or cloud inference.

9. Super Intelligence / AI-Assisted Development Disclosure

OpenAI ChatGPT was used to assist with software implementation, technical drafting, interface development, documentation, and aspects of algorithm design. Scientific assumptions, calculations, references, and generated outputs require independent verification and are documented with their respective limitations.

This project is an independent team prototype and does not claim NASA endorsement or flight qualification.
